stages.title: Complexity & maths basics
stages.summary: Learn to read a problem's limits and estimate time and space before writing code, using small number puzzles to practise.

patterns.title: Working with digits
patterns.idea: Peel digits off with % 10 and / 10; most digit problems are a loop over that pair.

patterns.title: Divisors, primes and GCD
patterns.idea: Check divisors only up to the square root, and use Euclid's algorithm for GCD in logarithmic time.

patterns.title: Simple loops and simulation
patterns.idea: Translate the statement into a loop exactly; these warm-ups train careful reading and edge cases.

patterns.title: Fast arithmetic
patterns.idea: Halve the search or the exponent each step: binary search for square roots, repeated squaring for powers.

stages.title: Arrays
stages.summary: Arrays reward scanning once and remembering the right thing: a pointer, a running sum or the best answer so far.

patterns.title: Single pass and in-place
patterns.idea: Keep a write pointer and overwrite as you read, so the array is fixed up in one pass with O(1) extra space.

patterns.title: Two pointers from both ends
patterns.idea: On sorted data, move the left or right pointer depending on whether the current sum is too small or too big.

patterns.title: Prefix sums
patterns.idea: Precompute running totals so any range sum is one subtraction, turning repeated O(n) work into O(1).

patterns.title: Best subarray (Kadane)
patterns.idea: At each index decide: extend the previous run or start fresh here. Track the best seen.

patterns.title: Counting and partitioning
patterns.idea: Voting and three-way partitioning solve majority and colour-sorting problems in one pass.

patterns.title: 2D arrays
patterns.idea: Walk a matrix by layers or swap across the diagonal; most matrix tricks are index arithmetic done carefully.

stages.title: Hashing
stages.summary: Trade memory for speed: a hash map answers 'have I seen this?' in constant time.

patterns.title: Seen-before lookups
patterns.idea: Store what you have visited; the moment you need its partner, look it up instead of searching.

patterns.title: Frequency counting
patterns.idea: Count characters or values into a map, then compare or sort the counts.

patterns.title: Grouping by a key
patterns.idea: Pick a key that is identical for items that belong together, like sorted letters, then bucket by it.

patterns.title: Prefix sums with a map
patterns.idea: Store how often each running sum has appeared; a target subarray exists when sum - k was seen before.

stages.title: Strings
stages.summary: Strings are arrays of characters, plus parsing: most tasks combine two pointers, counting and careful building.

patterns.title: String basics
patterns.idea: Reverse, compare and split with indices rather than repeated concatenation, which is quadratic.

patterns.title: Palindromes
patterns.idea: Expand around every centre, odd and even, to find palindromic pieces in O(n²) without extra space.

patterns.title: Parsing and building
patterns.idea: Handle signs, spaces and overflow explicitly, and build output with a list or builder.

patterns.title: Pattern matching
patterns.idea: Know the brute-force search first, then how prefix tables (KMP) avoid re-checking characters.

stages.title: Sorting & binary search
stages.summary: Sorted order unlocks binary search: discard half the candidates with every comparison.

patterns.title: Sorting as a tool
patterns.idea: Sort first when order makes the rest easy, and know merge sort well enough to write it from memory.

patterns.title: Classic binary search
patterns.idea: Keep an invariant on [lo, hi] and shrink it every step; most bugs are in the loop condition.

patterns.title: First and last positions
patterns.idea: Search for the first index where a condition becomes true; that one template covers bounds and peaks.

patterns.title: Rotated sorted arrays
patterns.idea: One half is always sorted; check whether the target falls inside it and discard the other half.

patterns.title: Binary search on the answer
patterns.idea: When you can check 'is answer x feasible?' quickly, binary search over x instead of over the array.

patterns.title: Searching a 2D matrix
patterns.idea: Treat a sorted matrix as one long array, or walk from a corner where one move always rules out a row or column.

stages.title: Recursion & backtracking basics
stages.summary: Recursion solves a problem through a smaller copy of itself; backtracking explores choices and undoes them.
concepts: Base cases and the call stack

patterns.title: Thinking recursively
patterns.idea: Trust the smaller call: define what it returns, handle the base case, combine one step.

patterns.title: Subsets and subsequences
patterns.idea: At every element choose to take it or skip it; skip duplicates at the same depth to avoid repeats.

patterns.title: Combinations with a target
patterns.idea: Recurse with the remaining target and stop early once it goes negative.

patterns.title: Permutations and generation
patterns.idea: Build answers position by position, marking what is used and undoing the mark on the way back.

patterns.title: Backtracking on grids and boards
patterns.idea: Mark a cell as visited, explore its neighbours, then unmark; prune as soon as a constraint breaks.

stages.title: Linked lists
stages.summary: Linked lists test pointer discipline: draw the nodes and update links in the right order.

patterns.title: Basic operations
patterns.idea: A dummy node before the head removes most special cases when inserting or deleting.

patterns.title: Fast and slow pointers
patterns.idea: Move one pointer twice as fast: they meet inside a cycle, and the slow one stops at the middle.

patterns.title: Reversal
patterns.idea: Reverse with three pointers (prev, cur, next); reversing a section is the same loop with careful reconnection.

patterns.title: Merging and sorting
patterns.idea: Merge two sorted lists with a dummy tail; merge sort on lists needs no extra array.

patterns.title: Lists with maps and stacks
patterns.idea: A map from old node to new node makes deep copies easy; caches pair a list with a map.

patterns.title: Doubly linked lists
patterns.idea: Keep both prev and next correct on every insert and delete; draw before and after states.

stages.title: Stacks & queues
stages.summary: Stacks remember the most recent unfinished thing; queues process work in arrival order.

patterns.title: Stack and queue basics
patterns.idea: Use a stack whenever the latest item must be matched or undone first, as with brackets.

patterns.title: Monotonic stacks
patterns.idea: Keep the stack sorted; popping finds each element's next greater or smaller value in O(n) overall.

patterns.title: Expressions and decoding
patterns.idea: Push numbers and pending operators, and resolve them when precedence or a closing bracket says so.

patterns.title: Stack simulation
patterns.idea: Let the stack hold survivors: compare each new item with the top and pop while it loses.

patterns.title: Queues and circular buffers
patterns.idea: A fixed array with head and tail indices that wrap around gives an O(1) queue with no shifting.

stages.title: Sliding window
stages.summary: Grow a window on the right and shrink it on the left so every element enters and leaves once.

patterns.title: Fixed-size windows
patterns.idea: Add the element entering and remove the one leaving instead of recomputing the whole window.

patterns.title: Variable-size windows
patterns.idea: Expand until the window breaks the rule, then shrink from the left until it is valid again.

patterns.title: Counting subarrays
patterns.idea: Count windows with 'at most k' and subtract to get 'exactly k'.

patterns.title: Harder windows
patterns.idea: Track what the window still needs with a counter map, or keep window maxima in a deque.

stages.title: Trees
stages.summary: Most tree problems are one traversal where each node combines what its children return.

patterns.title: DFS traversals
patterns.idea: Write preorder, inorder and postorder recursively and with an explicit stack.

patterns.title: Level order (BFS)
patterns.idea: Process the queue one level at a time by noting its size before the inner loop.

patterns.title: Heights and paths
patterns.idea: Return the best path through a child to the parent, and update a global best with both children.

patterns.title: Comparing and reshaping
patterns.idea: Recurse on both subtrees at once to compare or mirror them.

patterns.title: Ancestors and views
patterns.idea: Find the lowest common ancestor where the two targets split; record coordinates for vertical views.

patterns.title: Building and serialising
patterns.idea: The root comes first in preorder; its position in inorder splits the left and right subtrees.

stages.title: Binary search trees
stages.summary: Use the ordering: every decision goes left or right, so operations cost the tree's height.

patterns.title: Search, insert, delete
patterns.idea: Walk down comparing with each node; deleting a node with two children swaps in its successor.

patterns.title: Validation and order
patterns.idea: An inorder walk visits values in sorted order, so validation and k-th smallest follow directly.

patterns.title: Building BSTs
patterns.idea: Choose the middle as root to stay balanced; use value bounds to rebuild from a preorder walk.

stages.title: Heaps
stages.summary: A heap keeps the smallest or largest item ready in O(log n), ideal for top-k and scheduling.

patterns.title: Top-k elements
patterns.idea: Keep a heap of size k: the k best survive and the root is the k-th best.

patterns.title: Merging k sorted sources
patterns.idea: Put the head of each source in a min-heap and repeatedly take the smallest.

patterns.title: Two heaps
patterns.idea: A max-heap for the lower half and a min-heap for the upper half keep the median at the tops.

patterns.title: Scheduling with heaps
patterns.idea: Always pick the best available task, and push the ones you postpone back for later.

stages.title: Greedy & intervals
stages.summary: Make the locally best choice and prove it never hurts; with intervals, sort first.

patterns.title: Local best choices
patterns.idea: Ask what the best next move is, and check that a counter-example cannot beat it.

patterns.title: Sort, then be greedy
patterns.idea: Sorting reveals the order in which decisions become safe, as when pairing the heaviest with the lightest.

patterns.title: Intervals
patterns.idea: Sort by start (or end), then merge, insert or count overlaps in one pass.

stages.title: Graphs
stages.summary: Model the problem as nodes and edges, then choose BFS, DFS, topological order, union-find or Dijkstra.

patterns.title: Connected regions
patterns.idea: Run DFS or BFS from every unvisited cell or node; each start discovers one component.

patterns.title: Shortest steps with BFS
patterns.idea: On unweighted graphs BFS reaches nodes in order of distance; start from every source at once when there are many.

patterns.title: Topological order and cycles
patterns.idea: Process nodes with no remaining prerequisites; anything left over is part of a cycle.

patterns.title: Union-find and MST
patterns.idea: Union-find merges groups in near O(1); add the cheapest safe edges for a minimum spanning tree.

patterns.title: Weighted shortest paths
patterns.idea: Dijkstra pops the closest unsettled node from a heap; Floyd-Warshall handles all pairs on small graphs.

patterns.title: Colouring and bipartite checks
patterns.idea: Try to two-colour the graph with BFS; a same-colour edge proves it cannot be split.

stages.title: Dynamic programming
stages.summary: Define a state, write how it is built from smaller states, then compute each state once.

patterns.title: 1D DP
patterns.idea: The answer at i depends on a few earlier answers; start with the recursion, then fill an array.

patterns.title: 2D and grid DP
patterns.idea: Each cell combines the cells it can be reached from; fill row by row.

patterns.title: DP on two strings
patterns.idea: dp[i][j] compares prefixes of both strings; match, skip one, or edit.

patterns.title: Knapsack and subset sums
patterns.idea: For each item decide take or skip against a remaining capacity.

patterns.title: Increasing subsequences
patterns.idea: For each element, extend the best sequence that ends at a smaller earlier element.

patterns.title: Buy and sell states
patterns.idea: Track a few states per day, such as holding or not, and transition between them.

patterns.title: Interval and partition DP
patterns.idea: Try every split point of a range and combine the best answers of the two sides.

patterns.title: DP on trees
patterns.idea: Each node returns a small tuple of best answers, such as with and without itself, to its parent.

stages.title: Tries
stages.summary: A trie stores strings by shared prefixes, so prefix lookups cost the word length, not the word count.

patterns.title: Building a trie
patterns.idea: Each node holds children and an end-of-word flag; insert and search walk one character per level.

patterns.title: Tries for word search
patterns.idea: Search many words at once by walking the trie and the grid together.

patterns.title: Bitwise tries
patterns.idea: Store numbers bit by bit from the top; to maximise XOR, prefer the opposite bit at each level.

stages.title: Bit manipulation
stages.summary: Treat integers as bit arrays: masks test, set and clear bits, and XOR cancels pairs.

patterns.title: Bit basics
patterns.idea: x & (x - 1) clears the lowest set bit; most counting problems repeat that step.

patterns.title: XOR and arithmetic tricks
patterns.idea: XOR cancels equal values; count bits per position when numbers appear three times.

patterns.title: Bitmasks
patterns.idea: Represent a set of up to ~20 items as an integer and iterate over all masks.

stages.title: Mixed interview sets
stages.summary: Combine patterns under time pressure, the way real interviews do.

patterns.title: Design a data structure
patterns.idea: Choose the structures that make every required operation fast, then keep them in sync.

patterns.title: Mixed mediums
patterns.idea: No hint about the topic: read, choose the pattern, and justify the complexity.

patterns.title: Hard finals
patterns.idea: Break hard problems into known pieces before writing any code.
